plugins.name: zaksak
plugins.description: A collection of Claude Code utilities by Zak Sakata.

plugins.name: spec-ops
plugins.description: Retired. A spec-driven workflow that wrote, refined, launched and verified acceptance-criteria-first specs with a Claude and Codex judge. It is superseded by an outcome-first loop and stays listed only because gh-projects still delegates issue writing to it.

plugins.name: ralph
plugins.description: Retired 2026-11-19: use Claude Code's built-in /goal and /loop. Ralph Loop — an autonomous agentic coding workflow with sandbox isolation, scoped memory, and self-managing task iteration.

plugins.name: skill-manager
plugins.description: Retired 2026-11-19: no longer used. Manage your Claude Code skills and plugins from inside any project — switch which plugins are active, publish and sync local skills to a central marketplace, and diagnose and auto-repair a broken setup. Adapts to any repo layout and delegates skill authoring to the native skill-creator.

plugins.name: worktree-ops
plugins.description: Retired 2026-11-19: use Claude Code's built-in worktree support. A git worktree workflow for running multiple Claude Code sessions in parallel — no restarts, no manual checkouts. Built on native worktrees, it covers the full lifecycle from spinning up an isolated worktree to finishing it through a guarded, never-squashed PR merge, with a live dashboard of in-flight work and deterministic guards against squash merges and committing unresolved conflicts.

plugins.name: gh-projects
plugins.description: Run a small team's entire software lifecycle on GitHub Projects v2 — deterministic, free, GitHub-native, and with no metered AI. It provisions a golden-template board and repo automation across an org, then drives work from issue intake through sprint planning and the full branch → PR → merge flow with check-gated, never-squashed merges, kept safe by GitHub App-token writes and skill-scoped guards.

plugins.name: codex
plugins.description: Run the OpenAI Codex CLI from inside Claude Code as a cross-model escape hatch: hand a one-off review, question, or write task to a different provider's model for a second opinion, grounded in your repo with web search always on. Every call routes through one fail-open bridge — if Codex is absent, unauthenticated, or broken the skill reports and stops rather than answering as Claude, and Codex's output is surfaced verbatim as untrusted external text. Assumes an OpenAI-authenticated Codex setup.

plugins.name: statusline-band
plugins.description: A mod that ports the statuslineV4.sh status line into the band above the prompt, so the Claude Desktop Code tab, which runs no statusLine scripts, gets the same figures in two colored rows: directory, git branch, model and effort, with duration, version and session id on the right; rate limits, context, cost and output style, with RAM on the right. It stays off in the terminal by default, where the real status line still runs.

plugins.name: study
plugins.description: A study coach for books, papers and lecture decks built on retrieval practice. You read a few pages and recall them from memory; Claude grades the recall against the actual pages with page citations and asks follow-up questions, then drafts at most 8 flashcards aimed at what you missed. Cards reach Anki through AnkiConnect only after you approve each one.
